summary: Fixes a general once-per-turn ability architecture gap flagged from a playtest report (issue #126, part of bug 3's Doji Atsumichi investigation): Doji Atsumichi's and Shinjo Horibe's printed bow-or-straighten ability was modeled as two catalog entries (bow, straighten), each independently tracked in AbilityUses -- so the card could bow one target AND separately straighten another in the same turn, when the printed ability is really a single once-per-turn choice between two effects. Added AbilityDefinition.UsageKey: when set, the once-per-turn dedupe check and the per-use write key on it instead of the ability's own id, so multiple catalog entries can share one use. Applied to horibe-bow/horibe-straighten and atsumichi-bow/atsumichi-straighten; every other ability defaults UsageKey to its own id (unchanged behavior). This likely explains part of the originally reported 'personality bowed shortly after entering play, not called to pay a cost' symptom: an opponent's Atsumichi could bow a newly-recruited lower-Honor personality via one call, then (separately) straighten and re-bow other targets in the same turn well beyond the printed once-per-turn limit.
validation: Extended ShinjoHoribeBowOrStraighten and DojiAtsumichiBowOrStraighten (tests/L5R.Core.Tests/Program.cs) to assert that using one half of the ability blocks the other half, same turn, even against a different target. Full suite: 85/85 + 33/33 + 8/8 pass. bash tools/check.sh --skip-client passes (5/5 server integration, 4/4 client transport).
remaining: Bug 3 (attachments visually overlaying their Personality before settling) is still open. This does not claim to fully explain the original bowed-personality report -- the user should watch for a recurrence now that this specific defect is fixed.
